legend: Monocarp the Cook works in a large restaurant. He can cook two types of dishes: soup and dumplings. He likes to cook soup more — he spends one unit of energy to cook a soup serving and two units of energy to cook a dumpling serving. Soup and dumplings have different shelf life times:
a soup serving must be consumed either on the same day it is cooked or on the next day;
a dumpling serving can be stored for an infinite amount of days, so it can be consumed on any day, starting from the day it is cooked.

The restaurant is open for $$$n$$$ consecutive days. During the $$$i$$$-th day, there will be $$$a_i$$$ visitors in the restaurant. Monocarp should give either a serving of soup or a serving of dumplings to each visitor. Monocarp can serve any dish at his discretion. He can also serve different dish types during the day. The only requirement is that the dish's shelf life must be within allowed limits:
if a soup serving is given on day $$$1$$$, it must have been cooked on the same day;
if a soup serving is given on day $$$i  \gt  1$$$, it must have been cooked on day $$$i - 1$$$ or on day $$$i$$$;
if a dumpling serving is given on day $$$i$$$, it may have been cooked on any day between $$$1$$$ and $$$i$$$ inclusive.

Every day Monocarp starts with the same amount of energy $$$E$$$ — that is, he can cook any amount of soup and dumplings as long as the total energy he spends during each day is not greater than $$$E$$$. It is impossible to "conserve" energy — for example, if $$$E = 1$$$, Monocarp cannot choose to do nothing on one day and cook a serving of dumplings on the next day.

Monocarp would like to know the minimum possible amount of energy $$$E$$$ which he needs to have at the beginning of every day (same for each day) that would be enough to feed all visitors if he cooks dishes optimally.
input: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of consecutive days the restaurant is open.
The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$), where $$$a_i$$$ is the number of visitors during the $$$i$$$-th day.
output: Print one integer — the minimum amount of energy Monocarp needs to be able to cook enough dishes for all visitors.

legend.ai: 厨师 Monocarp 在一家大型餐厅工作。他会烹饪两种菜肴：汤和饺子。他更喜欢烹饪汤，因为烹饪一份汤需要消耗一个单位的能量，而烹饪一份饺子需要消耗两个单位的能量。汤和饺子的保质期不同：
一份汤必须在烹制当天或次日食用；
一份饺子可以无限期储存，因此从烹饪当天开始，它可以在任意一天食用。
这家餐厅将连续营业 $$$n$$$ 天。在第 $$$i$$$ 天，餐厅将有 $$$a_i$$$ 位顾客。Monocarp 应为每位顾客提供一份汤或一份饺子。Monocarp 可以自行决定提供哪种菜肴，也可以在一天内提供不同种类的菜肴。唯一的要求是，菜肴的保质期必须在允许范围内：
如果一份汤在第 $$$1$$$ 天供应，那么它必须在当天烹饪；
如果一份汤在第 $$$i  \gt  1$$$ 天供应，那么它必须是在第 $$$i - 1$$$ 天或第 $$$i$$$ 天烹制的；
如果一份在第 $$$i$$$ 天供应的饺子，它可能是在第 $$$1$$$ 天至第 $$$i$$$ 天(含首尾)之间的任意一天烹制的。
每天 Monocarp 都以相同的能量 $$$E$$$ 开始一天——也就是说，只要他每天消耗的总能量不超过 $$$E$$$，他就可以烹饪任意数量的汤和饺子。能量无法“储存”——例如，如果 $$$E = 1$$$，Monocarp 不能选择某一天什么都不做，然后在第二天烹饪一份饺子。
Monocarp 想知道，每天开始时他至少需要拥有多少能量 $$$E$$$(每天相同)，才能在最优烹饪菜肴的情况下为所有访客提供食物。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 $$$n$$$($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$)，表示餐厅连续营业的天数。
第二行包含 $$$n$$$ 个整数 $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$($$$0 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$)，其中 $$$a_i$$$ 表示第 $$$i$$$ 天的访客数量。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——Monocarp 为能够为所有访客烹饪足够的菜肴所需的最少能量。
